html:
The Salang Tunnel is a road tunnel about 2.7 km long through the Hindu Kush at the Salang Pass, about 90 km north of Kabul, built by the Soviet Union and opened in 1964. At nearly 3,400 metres it was long one of the highest road tunnels in the world.

Before it, traffic between Kabul and northern Afghanistan went far around or over high passes closed in winter. The tunnel cut the trip to a day and tied the north to the capital. It was a showpiece of Soviet aid in the Cold War, when Afghanistan took help from both Moscow and Washington.

That road became the main supply line of the Soviet invasion from 1979, and a target for the mujahideen of Ahmad Shah Massoud, whose Panjshir valley lay close by. In 1982 a fire in the tunnel killed many Soviet soldiers and Afghans, at least scores and perhaps far more. Damaged in later fighting, it reopened in 2002 and remains vital but dangerous, prone to avalanches, jams and fumes. The singer Ahmad Zahir died on the road near the pass in 1979.
